title: S&P 500 STOCK PRICE PREDICTION USING TECHNICAL, FUNDAMENTAL AND TEXT DATA

claims.description: Primary reported result for S&P 500 STOCK PRICE PREDICTION USING TECHNICAL, FUNDAMENTAL AND TEXT DATA
claims.target: directional prediction of stock price movement (up/down)

evidence_graph.quote: S&P 500 S TOCK PRICE PREDICTION USING TECHNICAL , FUNDAMENTAL AND TEXT DATA

A 66.18% accuracy in S&P 500 index directional prediction and 62.09% accuracy in individual stock directional prediction was achieved by combining different machine learning models such as Random Forest and LSTM together into state-of-the-art ensemble models.
A 66.18% accuracy in S&P 500 index directional prediction and 62.09% accuracy in individual stock directional prediction
518 different common stocks issued by current and former S&P 500 large-cap companies, from January 1, 2000 to December 31, 2019
we took the median sentiment each week for each company (with weeks ending on Fridays) as the sentiment variables in our weekly data
combined them with technical indices, fundamental characteristics and text-based sentiment data to predict S&P stock prices
combining different machine learning models such as Random Forest and LSTM together into state-of-the-art ensemble models
we chose the "bert-base-uncased" tokenizer to clean the text
Linear Regression models trained together using all stock's data

We used three years of information as training data. After two years of training data were input, the individual model predicts future observations iteratively, calculates the prediction errors and updates the model at the end of each year based on these errors. Also starting from the third year, the ensemble models were fitted using past years' prediction outputs as inputs to the ensemble model.

carefully selecting the corresponding predictor variables to control the number of input variables; training the machine learning algorithm across different stocks simultaneously then fine-tuning on each individual stock; creating an ensemble of models trained with different groups of stocks; and allowing multiple input and output periods for the LSTM model for more recursive training
A 66.18% accuracy in S&P 500 index directional prediction and 62.09% accuracy in individual stock directional prediction
The data we use contains weekly historical prices, finance reports, and text information from news items associated with 518 different common stocks
In our dataset which contains over 500 stocks and 3.2 million news items
Of the 170,779 extracted articles, 23,469 were positive, 37,426 were negative, and 109,884 were neutral.
